findings.text: The first paragraph tells a newcomer what Athena is, who it is for and what problem it solves, in plain words. This part works well.
findings.source: "Athena is an open-source system, written in Rust, that turns a short request into a change to a code repository... It solves the problem of AI edits that arrive unreviewed and unaccountable."

findings.text: The title is about a different project, firstmate, so someone arriving at Athena's home page may think they are on the wrong site. The lede has to explain that this page is a sample study before the title makes sense.
findings.source: Title and h1: "Athena explains how firstmate handles work"

findings.text: The first section after the navigation is a failure message. It sits exactly where the lede's promise of traceable models, cost and verdict should be shown, and it tells the newcomer that the proof is missing.
findings.source: Check it on a real job: "The records of job 20261029-073603-7kqv could not be read here, so no models, verdict or costs are shown: no reading record for job 20261029-073603-7kqv."

findings.text: This link is addressed to the site owner but sits in the header next to the newcomer's next step. A first-time reader has no proposals and will not know what it means.
findings.source: "Owner view: proposals waiting for your decision."

findings.text: The page links to the next step from the top, and the Next steps section gives concrete commands (git clone, ./setup.sh, athena ask "add a changelog") plus a prerequisite list. A newcomer knows what to do next.
findings.source: "Next step: install Athena or read firstmate itself" and the Next steps section

findings.text: Cargo is mentioned, but neither Rust nor cargo is in the prerequisite list, and the page does not say whether setup.sh installs them. The page also says nothing about the model access or spending the run will need, although Athena records what each step costs.
findings.source: Next steps: "a C linker (cc), which cargo needs to build Athena"

findings.text: The page does not warn that this changes the current repository, and does not suggest trying it on a scratch repository first.
findings.source: Next steps: "press Enter to run it on that repository"

findings.text: Even the default core track is dense with exit codes and internal terms (unheld, guarded fast-forward, captain call). A newcomer who has never heard of firstmate will struggle to follow the study, even though it is meant to show what Athena can do.
findings.source: One piece of work, start to finish: "If every place of a declared capacity is held, the spawn exits 75 and the item stays queued."

findings.text: It is honest that several terms are left undefined. But it leaves gaps that make the sample study harder to follow.
findings.source: Glossary: "The firstmate source does not define a captain call." (similar entries for durable record, endpoint, heartbeat, wake)

findings.text: Every statement links to a claim, and every claim links to pinned source lines. This clearly shows the traceability that Athena claims, which helps a newcomer see why it matters.
findings.source: "Each statement below ends with the id of the claim that supports it; the claims, with links to their sources, are listed at the end."
